text:
samir: Brain dump: lightweight two-pass prefill for draft-model onboarding. Calling it 'prefill-handoff-v0' here. Goal: punch up throughput on q-format models with minimal longform regressions.

claire: drop notes pls.

samir: Pasting quick runbook + eval sketch. TL;DR: cheap prefill (2-6 tokens) + confidence proxy -> selective full decode. Offline sims on a mix of 8k prompts look promising, esp for 13b and 14b quant variants.

samir: Motivation
- Repeated KV compute across sampling beams is common, esp on short token windows.
- Cheap prefill lets us avoid full decode for N/ D of requests.
- We can tune lookahead size and proxy threshold per route.

natalie: How do you pick proxy? is it model-internal score or an external estimator?

samir: Implementation sketch
- Prefill: sample L tokens via cheap config (e.g., temp 0.8, top_p 0.9) with lower kv fidelity (quant-friendly path). Keep M best partial traces.
- Proxy: combine short-run logprob avg + prefix-kv-hit proxy (cheap sim of cache reuse). If proxy > T -> accept prefill; else mark for full decode.
- Handoff: when full decode runs, we reinitialize KV and replay prefix deterministically from best prefill trace (reuse where safe).

claire: Ops concerns: how much extra memory for storing partial traces? When does the bookkeeping outweigh savings?

samir: Memory: store K trace candidates per request (~K * L * token_size). On our infra with batch sizes ~64 this was fine. Bookkeeping cost grows with concurrency but it's smaller than full KV copies in most cases.

dmitri: Preliminary numbers?

samir: Quick offline table (sim tokens/s, mixed batch, warm caches):
```
Model        | baseline tps | prefill tps | rel
rlh-13b-q4    | 1100         | 2100        | 1.91x
rlh-14b-q5    | 980          | 1820        | 1.86x
rlh-70b-q4    | 340          | 510         | 1.50x
```
Quality (coherence rerank diff, lower better):
- 13b: -0.28 relative (worse)
- 14b: -0.22 relative (worse)
- 70b: -0.45 relative on >2k token prompts
Std dev: ~0.04 across seeds.

claire: That's similar to what group has seen before. We should be careful on p95/p99 latency impact for customer-facing routes.

samir: Agreed. Observed p99 increase around ~10-15% in our microbench (because re-rolls can double work for some requests). Idea: policy per route: throughput-enable for background batch jobs, strict-no-prefill for low-latency routes.

yasmin: Safety/regressions: run both the automated safety classifier and a small human sweep. Also include regressive ngram checks for faithfulness on summarization.

samir: Will add safety scanner. Also planning a small A/B with our internal summarization partner (martech team) — Claire can coordinate.

opsbot: canary-scheduler: queued prefill-handoff-v0 canary on dedicated pool (ETA 2026-04-02 09:30 UTC).

dmitri: A couple notes: 1) please log per-request decisions (prefill-accepted, prefill-rejected, re-roll reason) for first 48h; 2) include trace IDs so we can replay problematic requests.

samir: good call. Will add telemetry tags and a replay hook.

natalie: Experiment variants to run (suggested)
- L in {2,4,6}
- K in {1,2,3}
- T threshold sweep (0.1 steps) on proxy score
- dataset mixes: longform-coherence (5k), summarization (3k), conv-short (10k)

claire: For canary criteria: stop and rollback if
- safety classifier FP rises > 0.5% absolute OR
- rerank coherence drop > 0.4 relative OR
- p99 latency regress > 20% on customer routes

samir: Action items:
- samir: push code + lightweight harness to /shared/onboard/prefill-handoff by EOD.
- dmitri: prepare telemetry dashboard + replay pipeline.
- natalie: prepare eval CSV spec and seeds.
- claire: own canary gating + coordinate customer A/B.
- yasmin: draft safety checklist + rater plan (200 longform prompts).

claire: One more ops question: how to handle multi-tenant cache safety? do we ever leak prefill traces between requests?

samir: No. Prefill traces are per-request and never shared across tenants. We do reuse model kernels and amortize KV ops within the same request only.

claire: OK good. Thanks for the writeup. I'll sign off once artifacts are live. :thumbsup:

samir: Thanks. Ping me for access.
